passage:
The rulebook came first. Himani marked the event date on the wall calendar and counted backward: rehearsal in the last week, testing before that, then the build, then design. Nobody had to guess where the team should be by now.

At the design meeting Tushar and Darshan filled twenty sticky notes with robot ideas, laughing at some, and nobody was allowed to say no yet. Then they scored each note on cost, time and what the three of them already knew. A plain line-follower won, with three sensors spaced in a clever arc.

The night before the competition, Tushar could not sit still. "What if it also picked up the little cubes?" He rewrote the control code until midnight and skipped the test run. In the first round the robot twitched at the first curve and rolled off the line while the crowd watched.

They finished fifth. The next Saturday Darshan brought a marker and a fresh sheet. Under one heading went the sensor idea and the calendar; under another, the wobbly calibration. Himani copied the changes for next year onto the last page of the notebook and added a date to look at them again.

qa.q: How many ideas did Tushar and Darshan put on sticky notes?
qa.a: They filled twenty sticky notes with robot ideas.

qa.q: How did the team's early planning differ from what happened the night before the competition?
qa.a: Early on the calendar and the scored notes kept each choice tied to the plan, but the midnight code rewrite skipped the test run and the robot rolled off the line in the first round.

qa.q: What was Tushar probably feeling as the robot rolled off the line?
qa.a: Dismay and regret, because the untested rewrite that had seemed exciting the night before caused the failure.

qa.q: What could the team do at next year's event to avoid a repeat?
qa.a: They could stop changing the code before the last week and test any new feature fully, or save it for after the event.

grounding: Four approaches to preparing for a robotics competition: working backward from the date, brainstorming then selecting, untested last-minute changes, and learning from the result.
